title: SLO maturity matrix and dashboard consolidation roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a company-wide SLO maturity matrix and a two-phase dashboard consolidation roadmap for the Redwood platform. The goal is to reduce SLI definition drift, simplify operator workflows, and provide a clear operator enablement pathway so oncall engineers and operators can reliably interpret service health and execute remediation steps.

Goals
- Harmonize SLI definitions across core runtime services (runtime-allocator, prefix-cache, tenant-router, batching-engine).
- Consolidate dashboards to a single Grafana workspace per region with standardized panels and templating.
- Define SLO maturity levels and operator training milestones.
- Reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for latency and token-cost incidents by 30% within 6 months of phase 2 completion.

Scope and non-goals
- In-scope: Services that contribute directly to inference latency/cost and routing: runtime-allocator, prefix-cache, batching-engine, tenant-router, console-sli-service, telemetry-ingest.
- Out-of-scope: external third-party models and partner-managed gateways (handled in separate playbooks).

SLO maturity matrix (summary)

The maturity matrix below defines four levels for SLO definitions and telemetry coverage. Use this to prioritize work by service.

1) Level 0 — Ad-hoc
- No canonical SLI definitions. Alerts are handcrafted per-dashboard.
- Example state: separate teams interpret P95 differently (wall-clock vs. token-normalized).

2) Level 1 — Canonical SLIs defined
- Machine-readable SLI definitions published in console-sli-service (YAML).
- Basic dashboards exist, but panels are not templated.

3) Level 2 — Instrumented & audited
- SLIs wired to telemetry-ingest with consistent labels and units.
- Dashboards use templates and common panel library. Alert rules are codified in alert-repo.

4) Level 3 — Automated remediation & runbook links
- SLIs drive automated incident priority and playbook linking.
- Operator workflows include synthetic verification and automated prefilling of context bundles.

Prioritization table (text form)
- Tier A (high impact): runtime-allocator, prefix-cache — target Level 2 in Q1, Level 3 in Q2.
- Tier B (medium impact): batching-engine, tenant-router — target Level 2 in Q2, Level 3 in Q3.
- Tier C (low impact): console-sli-service, telemetry-ingest — target Level 1 in Q1, Level 2 in Q2.

Canonical SLI examples (intentional machine-readable snippet)
- Sample SLO YAML (to be checked into console-sli-service repo):

  # slo-definition: runtime-allocator/p95-latency.yaml
  name: allocator_p95_latency
  service: runtime-allocator
  sli: request_latency_ms_p95
  source: telemetry-ingest
  target: \"<= 120\" # milliseconds
  window: 30d
  objective: 0.995
  labels: [region, tenant_priority]

Note: We store these YAML files in git under infra/sli-definitions/ so they are versioned and part of pull request reviews.

Dashboard consolidation roadmap (high level)

Phase 1 — Inventory & canonicalization (6 weeks)
1. Inventory all Grafana dashboards and panel owners across us-west-2, eu-west-1. (Owner: telemetry-team).
2. For each dashboard, extract SLI expressions and map to canonical SLI names in console-sli-service.
3. Migrate metric queries to the canonical metric names (prometheus/remote-write selectors).
4. Deliverable: canonical-dashboard-inventory.csv with columns: service, dashboard_id, panel_id, canonical_sli, owner, notes.

Phase 2 — Consolidation & templating (10 weeks)
1. Create a centralized Grafana workspace per region. (Owner: observability-platform).
2. Implement a standardized panel library: latency, error-rate, token-rate, queue-depth, batch-fill.
3. Replace service-specific panels with templated panels referencing canonical SLI names.
4. Attach runbook links (runbook-url) and synthetic check buttons to each critical panel.
5. Deliverable: grafana-library v1.0, consolidated-workspace-{region}.

Phase 3 — Alert rationalization & automation (8 weeks)
1. Convert ad-hoc alerts to rule groups in alert-repo. Use the SLO-reconciler job to synthesize alert thresholds from SLOs.
2. Map alerts to PagerDuty escalation policies and include SLO context in the first notification.
3. Implement one-click incident creation that pre-populates: impacted tenants, recent prefetched keys, and relevant traces.

Ownership and timelines (text table)
- telemetry-team: inventory, labels normalization — Q1
- observability-platform: grafana consolidation, panel library — Q1–Q2
- runtime-team: instrument canonical SLIs for runtime-allocator — Q1
- caching-team: prefix-cache SLI instrumentation — Q1
- platform-ops: alert mapping and PagerDuty config — Q2

Runbook (operator-facing) — when a dashboard shows P95 latency breach
1. Verify canonical SLI: confirm the panel is pulling the right canonical metric (metric name and labels).
2. Check the last 15m of traffic and batch occupancy on batching-engine.
3. If batching-engine occupancy < 70% and request queues growing, escalate to runtime-team and apply temporary burst policy: `rdctl allocator apply-burst --pool=shared --duration=10m`.
4. If prefix-cache miss-rate > 8% and eviction rate spikes, trigger cache-drain-and-warmup: follow runbook `cache-drain-warmup-v2`.
5. Document the incident via incident template and link to the dashboard snapshot.

Alerting and SLO integration details
- SLO thresholds:
  - Latency (P95) primary objective: <= 120ms (objective 99.5% over 30d) for Tier-A customers.
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated capacity endpoints.
  - Error budget burn alert: trigger at 25%/7d (warning) and 75%/7d (pagerduty-critical).
- Alert mapping: alerts are derived from SLI query expressions using `slo-reconciler` that lives in infra/tools/slo-reconciler.

Migration checklist
- [ ] Inventory file committed and reviewed.
- [ ] All canonical SLIs defined in console-sli-service and approved via PR.
- [ ] Dashboards migrated to consolidated workspace with templated panels.
- [ ] Alert rules generated from SLOs and validated in staging.
- [ ] Operator runbooks linked on dashboard panels.
- [ ] Synthetic checks and one-click incident prefill tested in canary region.

Operator enablement and training pathway
- Week 0: Documentation review and quiz in the operator knowledge base.
- Week 1: Hands-on lab — simulate P95 degradation and run the runbook steps in the sandbox.
- Week 3: Certification exercise: perform a full mitigation and postmortem.
- Ongoing: Quarterly tabletop gamedays using consolidated dashboards.

KPIs and success criteria
- Reduce MTTR for SLO breaches by 30% within 6 months of phase 2 completion.
- 90% of Tier-A services at Level 2 maturity within 3 months.
- Zero SLI-definition drift incidents reported in quarterly audits.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Query semantics differ between regions (prometheus label differences).
  - Mitigation: Add query translation layer in telemetry-ingest; include unit tests in Grafana provisioning.
- Risk: Operator cognitive load during transition.
  - Mitigation: Provide training, cheat-sheets, and a paired oncall window.

Appendix: useful commands and locations
- Where SLI definitions live: git/src/infra/sli-definitions/
- SLO reconciler: infra/tools/slo-reconciler/README.md
- Grafana provisioning repo: infra/grafana/provisioning/
- Example: check P95 from CLI
  $ metrics query \"request_latency_ms_p95{service=\"runtime-allocator\",region=\"us-west-2\"}\" --window=15m
